correctness.rationale: For each real affine symbol, the Fourier transform formula and scaling give norm a_j^{-1/2}. The unitary logarithmic change of variable reduces positive-frequency action to shifts with unimodular offset factors that converge uniformly to one on packets escaping toward zero frequency. Exact overlaps imply the full-line scalar Mellin symbol norm for zero offsets. Weakly null translated packets prove the same lower bound for every compact perturbation and all offsets. The triangle-defect identity makes sharpness equivalent to a Kronecker phase orbit closure, and the character-annihilator criterion gives all integer relations. This proves the if-and-only-if uniformly in offsets and the flat approximation-number conclusion. The resonance norm 3 sqrt(5)/4 follows from exact maximization of an explicit concave quadratic. The standard-library packet checker was replayed and passed, but universal correctness rests on the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The exact if-and-only-if classifies when arbitrary real affine offsets cannot destroy triangle-bound equality for a natural multi-operator Hilbert Paley–Wiener sum. It also fixes all approximation numbers and provides an explicit genuine resonance loss with coefficient phases, explaining when arithmetic dependence matters. The generic-versus-resonant dichotomy is relevant to stability of combined bandlimited signal warps and operator approximability; it is neither a known-table recomputation nor a small numerical increment. The mathematical object and sharp invariant are intrinsically motivated even without a downstream theorem.
